Signatories on the roster issue it, which freezes it at a SHA-256 hash; issued documents are baselined as a set and exported to Word. The split matters for review. Facts from the workspace are checkable against the project. Engineering judgment, such as why a tool needs no qualification or how independence is achieved, is the part an auditor will question, so it is always drafted as a proposal and decided by a person. Prose fills in the rest. Open a document from the library, or create one with Create from template.

An open document has three tabs: Nodes shows the document's sections in order, read-only, with each section's UID. Text renders as Markdown, and Mermaid and Archify diagram blocks render as figures. Sections an agent drafted carry Proposed — awaiting review; accepted ones carry Decided. The document control page with its revision history sits at the top. Decisions · N is the queue of agent-drafted sections waiting for your review. Completion lists what stands between the document and its issue, and holds the Sign and issue button. The PSAC of the Canister copy in the Nodes tab: safety, resource, redundancy, timing and certification sections, each marked Decided once an engineer accepted it. Sections are not typed into directly. Text comes from the workspace, from the docs swarm, from accepted decisions, and from the answers you give in the Completion tab, so every sentence has a recorded source. From the workspace, no model. Sections whose content is a fact about the project, such as the toolchain, the source files, the target and the tools in use, are filled from the workspace when the document is created. Decisions, drafted by an agent. Select Propose decisions and an agent drafts each section that needs engineering judgment. Each draft is marked PROPOSED, awaiting engineer review and counts for nothing until a person accepts it. Prose, by the docs swarm. Write an instruction and select Run docs swarm, or use Author set… to author several documents in one go. Each section is saved as soon as it is written, so stopping and restarting picks up where it left off. Improve with model also revises the template prose.

When drafts are waiting, the document shows how many decisions await your review. Select Review decisions, pick yourself as the reviewer, and for each draft: Accept it as written, Edit and accept it with your changes, or Reject it with a comment that the next draft has to answer. If the fact check flags a draft, accepting it needs Accept over fact check…, so the override is on record. Every accepted decision is stored as a review and in the audit trail. Accept N routine accepts the routine drafts in one step. It never includes a draft marked safety-critical or one that contradicts another document; those are always decided one at a time.

When the project changes, a document's workspace facts go stale. The library marks it, and Regenerate stale (N) or a document's own regenerate icon builds a new version and shows it before anything is saved: every section is labelled Updated, Reset for re-authoring, Kept or Unchanged, with Show diff for a line-by-line comparison; an issued document is flagged because saving returns it to draft; Save as new revision archives the current revision first and saves the new one; Cancel changes nothing. Sections reset for re-authoring are written again by the docs swarm.

The Completion tab shows the document's state (Awaiting review, Open items remain, Ready to issue, Issued or Changed since issue), a progress bar, and four numbered lists: Agent proposals awaiting review, with a shortcut to the Decisions tab. Engineering decisions, answered by the Responsible engineer you name. Waiting for workspace evidence: facts the project has not produced yet. Refresh from workspace checks again; the engineer can also record them directly. Cross-document consistency: contradictions with other documents, each marked Blocks issue or Warning, which you fix or waive with a reason. When it is clear, choose a person from the roster for each approval role and select Sign and issue (baseline). The issued revision is frozen with a SHA-256 hash of its content, and the audit trail gets one entry for the baseline and one per signature. Later edits become a new revision: Record revision (enabled once the saved content differs from the last recorded version) asks "What changed since vx?" and records it. SVR and SAS cannot be issued until the latest compliance run shows that verification was executed. When the set is ready, Declare set baseline records the whole set against the current git commit.

Select Export .docx on a document, or Export all in the library. The export is a formal document with a cover page, contents, numbered headings, tables, and Mermaid and Archify figures rendered as images. To match your company's format, open Document template… and select Import from .docx… with one of your Word documents. Noyce IDE takes its styles, header and footer, page setup and logo, and suggests a cover. Save template applies it to every export; Reset to built-in goes back.

Read issued Word documents and certification packages in place, and edit standalone Word files. Open it with Noyce: Document Reader. The Document Reader's library: each document with its path and completion, for example ICD 13 of 13 sections complete and PSAC 90 of 98 with 8 open. Select a document to read it as the formal Word document it exports to: cover page, document control, numbered headings, tables and figures, with your template applied. The PSAC of the Canister copy in the Document Reader: the cover with its document number, revision, system and software level, marked DRAFT until it is approved. The library lists the DO-178C documents, Markdown and Word files the agents wrote under .noyce/, and certification packages. Read shows the page; Reload reads it from disk again. Edit opens a standalone Word file in an in-place editor with Save and Cancel. While the docs swarm is writing the open document, the page refreshes about every 12 seconds. NoteEdit is offered only for standalone .docx files. A generated document explains where it comes from and opens its source.

Markdown files (.md, .markdown) open in a WYSIWYG editor by default. Your edits go back into the file about a quarter of a second after you stop typing, so saving, the unsaved-changes dot and undo all work as usual, and changes made to the file elsewhere (for example a git checkout) appear in the editor. MISRA squiggles are not shown in this editor. PDF files open in the built-in viewer, which works offline: thumbnails, page navigation, zoom (⌘+ and ⌘−), rotate, find (⌘F, then Enter and ⇧Enter between matches), copy the file path, and open in your system viewer.

Every surface on this page measures your code with a real tool. When the tool is not installed or has not been run, the surface says so; it never shows sample results as yours. Install what you need from Optional tools. Surface Tool DO-178C MISRA Diagnostics cppcheck (MISRA addon) or clang-tidy A-5 Formal Verification CBMC 6.9.0 A-5, A-6 (analysis, not tests) Code Scanning CodeQL 2.25.6 A-5 MC/DC Coverage LLVM/Clang 18+ A-7 Data & Control Coupling Project graph A-7(8) Object Code Traceability arm-none-eabi-objdump A-7(9)

Coding-standard findings from every analyzer, in one list. Open it from the tile or Noyce Compliance: Open MISRA Diagnostics. Static Analysis on the Canister copy. The counts line explains itself: 1,532 project findings, 1,408 from cppcheck and 124 from the heuristic scan, which is marked not evidence. How to use it Select Scan. Noyce IDE runs cppcheck with the MISRA addon, or clang-tidy, and falls back to a built-in heuristic scan only when neither is installed. Filter by Severity (Mandatory, Required, Advisory) or by Tool. Select a finding to see its rule, its file and line, and the tool that reported it. Open in Editor jumps to the line. Fix with Noyce proposes a fix as a change set; see Review AI changes. To accept a finding instead, record a deviation in Evidence Records → MISRA deviations. Export Findings saves the list. The counts line is worth reading. On the Canister copy it says that 624 of 1,532 findings were stored, because the run stores at most 500 coding-standard findings per analyzer; no defect-class finding is ever dropped. ImportantHeuristic findings are marked not evidence and never count toward an objective. Install cppcheck for findings an auditor will accept.

Bounded model checking proves array bounds, arithmetic overflow and your assertions, or produces a counterexample. Open it from the CBMC Verification tile or Noyce Compliance: Open Formal Verification. Formal Verification on the Canister copy: no harnesses generated and no verification run yet. Install CBMC with Install CBMC in the view, or brew install cbmc. Select Generate harnesses to write one harness per code unit from your accepted low-level requirements: inputs bounded by each LLR's stated ranges, called functions stubbed from their prototypes, and the LLR's properties asserted. Harnesses are written to cbmc-harness/llr/ as a change set, so you approve them like any other code. Select Run Verification (or Run harnesses). Each property is reported as proved or failed with its trace. CBMC results are analysis: they support code review and never count as tests. A failed property can be sent to Fix with Noyce or turned into a problem report.

A semantic security scan that follows data from inputs through your code. Open it from the tile or Noyce Compliance: Open Code Scanning (CodeQL). Code Scanning on the Canister copy after a security-and-quality scan. The TI compiler cannot be traced, so the scan ran buildless and says so above the alert counts. Select Install CodeQL if it is not installed. Noyce IDE downloads the official CodeQL bundle and checks its SHA-256. Choose the query pack: security-extended or security-and-quality. Select Run scan. For TI Code Composer Studio projects the scan uses the include paths from the project's .cproject. How the code is extracted. CodeQL normally watches the project's build to see every file exactly as compiled. Its tracer cannot follow the TI armcl compiler, so a traced scan of a TI project extracts nothing. Noyce IDE then repeats the scan with --build-mode=none, which reads the sources directly and guesses include paths and defines. On the Canister firmware that extracts 21 of its 22 files. The dashboard always says how the database was built. A buildless or partial extraction is listed above the alert counts, so a count of 0 is never read as "no problems": only a traced scan that extracted every file is conclusive. Each alert shows its rule, severity and the data-flow path. Fixes go through change sets.

Statement, decision and modified condition/decision coverage, measured by running instrumented code. Open it from the tile or Noyce Compliance: Open MC/DC Coverage. MC/DC Coverage on the Canister copy: 109 conditions and 150 independence vectors found in the source; 0 of 9 modules measured, shown as a structural zero, not a result. Coverage is measured per module, with a test driver for each: Write a driver under tests/mcdc/ that exercises one source file, and name the file it covers in a comment: // @coverage-source ../AUTO_SEQUENCE.c. Pick the module and select Measure module. Noyce IDE builds it with LLVM's MC/DC instrumentation, runs the driver and reads the result. Each run is a background job you can cancel, with a five-minute limit. Generate Coverage Tests has an agent write and check tests for the decisions shown, and Fix Uncovered Decisions gives the decisions still missing independence pairs to the coding agent. Both open Agent output so you can follow the work. Until a module is measured, its obligations are counted and its coverage reads 0% with the note "a structural zero, not a result". NoteMC/DC needs LLVM/Clang 18 or newer. With only GCC and gcov installed you get statement and branch coverage, and MC/DC reads "unavailable".

Which components call and share data with which, and whether a requirement-based test exercises each coupling. Open it from the DC/CC Analysis tile. Data & Control Coupling on the Canister copy: 23 components, 65 uncovered couplings, measured against the 100% Level A threshold. On the Canister copy coupling coverage is shown as not measured: no executed requirement-based test exists yet, so no coupling can be counted as exercised. That is the honest state, not a failure of the tool.

For DO-178C A-7(9) at Level A: object code that no source line accounts for, such as soft-float helpers, C runtime start-up and the reset vector, each of which needs a named person's justification. Open it with Noyce Compliance: Open Object Code Traceability. Object Code Traceability before any analysis. LimitationThis view reads an analysis produced outside it: the view suggests npm run socta -- --project <path>, a script in the Noyce IDE source repository that is not available in the installed app. It needs a linked image and arm-none-eabi-objdump.

Finds the project's tests, runs them with Run All, drafts new ones with AI Generate, and records test runs on the target as verification evidence. Open it with ⌘⌥N then T. Test Explorer on the Canister copy, which has no Unity or C tests yet.

A software bill of materials from the project's real manifests, matched against known vulnerabilities and weaknesses. Open it from the tile. Cyber Assurance on the Canister copy: 3 components. No vulnerability database was queried, because none of them records a version, so the posture reads not assessed. Choose the standard (for example DO-326A / ED-202A) and select Analyze. CVE matching uses OSV and needs a network connection, and it matches by version: a component with no recorded version is not assessed rather than reported clean. Generate SBOM and Export Security Pack write the results.

Code-quality metrics computed in the IDE, with snapshots over time. Open it with ⌘⌥N then Q. Quality Trend on the Canister copy: 22 source files and 83 functions, maintainability 46 of 100, average cyclomatic complexity 7.7, highest 65. Capture Snapshot records today's numbers so later scans show the trend. The function list ranks functions by cyclomatic complexity; Fix with agent on a function hands it to an agent to reduce its complexity.

The catalogue of analyzers Noyce IDE can run, with what is installed and what is recommended for the project. Open it with Noyce Compliance: Open Analysis Tools. Analysis Tools: installed analyzers at the top, with Run Analysis; recommended and commercial tools below.

Noyce IDE builds a TI Code Composer Studio project with the TI compiler you have installed, without opening CCS. You can build the way you would in any other IDE, from a task and the status bar, or from the Build view, which shows the result in detail. What it can build. A project with a CCS .cproject at its root. Noyce IDE reads its build configurations, the declared compiler (TI ARM CGT armcl, TI Arm Clang tiarmclang or GNU Arm arm-none-eabi-gcc), the sources and the include paths. The Build view also builds STM32CubeIDE projects with a .cproject at the root or one folder down. How it finds the compiler. Your PATH first, then the TI install folders: ~/ti and /Applications/ti on macOS, C:\ti and %USERPROFILE%\ti on Windows. When several versions are installed, the newest is used. TivaWare is found automatically; other SDK locations come from the COM_TI_*_INSTALL_DIR and SW_ROOT environment variables. The IDE only runs compilers it found itself.

When the open folder has a CCS project, two items appear on the left of the status bar: the build configuration (for example Debug) and Build. To Do Build the selected configuration ⇧⌘B (CtrlShiftB on Windows), Build in the status bar, or Noyce Build: Build. Choose the configuration Select it in the status bar, or Noyce Build: Select Configuration. Delete this configuration's build output Noyce Build: Clean. Run a specific configuration Tasks: Run Task → Noyce Build → Noyce: Build Debug, Noyce: Build Release or Noyce: Clean …. The build runs as a task in the terminal panel, so the compiler output streams as it is produced and you can stop it like any other task. The status bar item then reads Built with the duration, Build failed with the error count, or Build cancelled. Compiler errors and warnings go to the Problems panel and are underlined in the editor. TI armcl diagnostics ("file.c", line 145: warning #994-D: …), fatal errors and remarks each have their own problem matcher; GNU builds use the standard $gcc matcher.

Open it from the Build Pipeline tile, Noyce Build: Open Build Pipeline or ⌘⌥N then B. The Build view on the Canister copy after a Debug build with TI armcl 20.2.6: errors, warnings, duration and image size along the top, and the compiler diagnostics with their file and line. Header: the project, the compiler found and its version, the last result, and Build. When something is missing, Build is disabled and a Build blocked panel lists each problem: the compiler, CG_TOOL_ROOT, or an SDK path that did not resolve. Configuration: the CCS build configuration to build. Errors, Warnings, Duration and Image size. Image size comes from the link map; Open Firmware Memory opens the full breakdown. Diagnostics: every error, warning and remark with its code. Select the file and line to open it. Diagnostics in vendor SDK files are marked vendor and listed after your own. Output: the full compiler output. Toolchain: the compiler path and version, the exact build command, its working directory, and the SDK variables used. Artifacts: the files the build wrote, with size and modified time. History: the latest stored CCS build of each configuration, with its result and duration. Every build is listed in the sidebar Build Status view (below).

Before it runs, the Build view checks that the CubeIDE makefiles only name paths that exist on this computer. Makefiles generated on another machine (a C:/… path on a Mac, for example) block the build. The Build blocked panel then offers Build with a generated makefile: Noyce IDE writes its own makefile from the .cproject and .ioc under .noyce/build/stm32-<configuration>/portable-build/ and builds with arm-none-eabi-gcc and make. It is not the CubeIDE build. When a compiler without its C library stops the build, the output starts with a hint naming the fix. When a build fails before reporting any error against a file and line, the Errors tile says so. A walkthrough of both paths is in Import and build. Which compiler. Set noyce.stm32.armToolchainPath to a toolchain's bin folder to choose the compiler. A tool in that folder wins over one on PATH: in Validate Toolchain, in the generated tasks (the folder goes first on their PATH), in the debug launch and in the Build view (passed to the generated makefile as GCC_PATH). Otherwise PATH is used, then STM32CubeIDE's bundled tools. The record keeps the compiler's measured version. The STM32 ⇧⌘B task that Regenerate Workspace Files writes is recorded the same way, with the compiler version it measured. Its output stays in the terminal and is not stored in the record. Each build-record.json holds only the latest build of its configuration. Every recorded build, CCS or STM32, also adds one line to .noyce/build/history.jsonl with its time, kind, project, configuration, exit code, duration and toolchain. The file keeps the last 200 builds. The sidebar Build Status view lists the newest 10, with the result, CCS or STM32, the duration and how long ago; hover one for the toolchain and exit code, or select it to open the Build view. A project built before history.jsonl existed shows the latest build of each configuration until its next build. NoteLinking happens only with armcl and a linker command file whose libraries all resolve; otherwise the build compiles only, and there is no .map or image size.

The Noyce build tasks have the task type noyce-ccs, so you can add your own to .vscode/tasks.json, for example to bind a Release build to a key: jsonCopy{ "version": "2.0.0", "tasks": [ { "type": "noyce-ccs", "configuration": "Release", "action": "build", "label": "Noyce: Build Release", "problemMatcher": ["$ti-armcl"] } ] } configuration is the CCS configuration name and action is build or clean.

Finds the project's C unit tests, runs them on your computer, and runs requirement-based tests on the target through a debug probe. Open it with ⌘⌥N then T. Test Explorer on the Canister copy, which has no Unity or C tests yet. The Run on target card is shown because a desktop host is connected. Unit tests on your computer Tests are found by scanning .c and .cpp files for TEST_CASE( or void test_… functions; each file is a suite. Run All compiles every test file, with Unity, into one program using your host gcc, runs it, and shows each test's result. If the project does not include Unity, the IDE's bundled copy is used from .noyce/unity/. It needs gcc and gcov on macOS or Linux. AI Generate has the Test Engineer agent write Unity tests for the active file, compiles and runs them, and makes one repair attempt if they fail. The generated tests are staged as a change set, not written into your project. Every Run All is recorded under .noyce/verification/test-runs/ with its run id. Requirement-based tests. Switch the right pane to By requirement and select Run tests. Noyce IDE runs your project's own test command (make test, or make in tests/ or test/) and seals the result under .noyce/verification/test-runs/. Run on target. Builds tests/target/*.c with the portable build, flashes it through a probe-rs probe (ST-Link, J-Link or CMSIS-DAP), verifies the flash, and reads TEST name reqs PASS|FAIL lines over RTT. Each run is recorded with the chip, probe, firmware SHA-256 and toolchain in .noyce/verification/target/runs/. It needs: an attached probe, portable-build/build-config.json with a linker script (select Generate portable build in Evidence Records → Change sets), at least one tests/target/<name>.c defining noyce_suite_<name>(), and a main() in the build. Nothing is recorded unless flashing finished and read back correctly.

Builds, flashes and checks your firmware with your own commands and, when a step fails, asks the coding agent for a repair. Open it with ⌘⌥N then V; Noyce Agents: Configure Firmware Validation Loop opens its settings. Setting Default noyce.agents.firmwareLoop.buildCommand none Required. Any shell command, run in the workspace folder. noyce.agents.firmwareLoop.flashCommand none Optional. noyce.agents.firmwareLoop.observeCommand none Optional, for example reading the serial port. noyce.agents.firmwareLoop.successPattern none Regular expression the observe output must match. noyce.agents.firmwareLoop.timeoutSeconds 120 Per command, 5 to 600. noyce.agents.firmwareLoop.autoApply off Skips the review prompt; the repair is still only staged. One run: build, then flash, then observe. A step fails on a non-zero exit, a timeout, or an observe output that does not match the pattern. On the first failure the coding agent receives the command, its output and the source files it names, and returns a patch. You review it and Stage for Review; it becomes a change set. It is never written to your files directly. Repairs iterate up to maxAttempts times in an isolated copy under .noyce/firmware-loop/trial, rebuilding there after each patch. One change set with the combined repair is staged, with how many attempts were made and whether the trial build passed. Flash and observe run only on your real workspace. NoteThe loop needs noyce.agents.enableShell; it asks before turning it on. Fix Build Errors with AI is the single-pass version: it takes the errors in the Problems panel (no build is run), asks the coding agent for fixes, and stages them as a change set with Stage all fixes or Stage per file….

Command Does Noyce STM32: Import CubeIDE Project Reads a .ioc or project folder and writes .vscode/tasks.json, launch.json, settings.json, extensions.json and compile_commands.json: a make build task, an OpenOCD flash task, a Cortex-Debug launch configuration, and clangd set up for the project. It also loads the pin configuration. Existing files of those names are overwritten. Regenerate Workspace Files Writes the same files again for the open folder. Validate Toolchain Checks arm-none-eabi-gcc, arm-none-eabi-gdb, openocd (required), make, cmake, STM32_Programmer_CLI and st-util, one line each, then says whether you can build, flash and debug and why not. A compiler without its C library (newlib) is reported as blocking the build. List Debug Probes Lists connected probes through probe-rs. Attach Debug Probe, Detach Debug Probe Attach to the target through probe-rs; the status bar shows the attached target. Read Target Memory, Start / Stop RTT Streaming Read memory and stream RTT into the "Noyce RTT" output. Memory reads, RTT and the STM32 Debug State view offer to attach when no probe is attached yet. Memory watches are kept across reloads.

Follow what each Orchestrator agent is doing and what it produced. Open it with Agent output in the Orchestrator. Agent Output on the Canister copy: one tab per agent, the tasks routed to the selected agent on the left, and the selected task's live output, reasoning, actions and run summary. One tab per agent, with a dot while it is running or waiting for your review, and its task count. The view follows the agent currently running. Workflow Tasks on the left: the tasks routed to that agent and their status. The selected task: the live output as it streams, Model reasoning (opens on its own while the model is thinking), Actions (each tool step, with steps that write files or run commands marked apart), and a Run summary with the outcome, tokens and time. Proposed file changes for the coding and test agents, with Stage all as change set or Stage per file. Nothing is written until the change set is approved and applied. The Trace agent's tab shows the project's linked-requirement ratio and measured MC/DC, or "Not measured".
Open any hardware surface from the Hardware activity bar icon, its tile on the start tab, or a Noyce Hardware: command.

Your microcontroller's reference manual, turned into a searchable register database where every fact cites the page it came from. Open it from the tile or Noyce Hardware: Open Register Knowledge. Register Knowledge on the Canister copy: the 1,892-page TM4C1294NCPDT datasheet indexed into 888 registers (654 with bit fields) and 592 documented rules. GPIOAFSEL is documented on page 770, with its offset, the base address of every GPIO port, and its bit fields. 01THE MANUAL02THE INDEXevery fact cites its page03YOUR FIRMWARE04WHAT YOU ASKPart detected on importTM4C1294 · STM32G4 …Reference manual PDFdownloaded, or Choose PDF…knowledge/<doc>.jsonregisters: offset, reset valuebit fieldsbase address of every instancerules: unlock, commit, orderingpage number on eachRe-index rebuilds itDirect register writesGPIO_PORTF_AFSEL_R = …Through the vendor HALGPIOPinTypeUART → AFSELLink codeRegister + fieldswith the page it is onWhere code writes itfile:line, direct or via HALBuild graphRules ↔ registers ↔ codeone connected graphThe manual and the index live in .noyce/manuals/ and .noyce/knowledge/ and are not committed; re-run Re-index after replacing the PDF. The manual for the detected part is downloaded or chosen, then indexed into registers, bit fields, base addresses and rules, each citing its page. Link code finds where your firmware writes each register, directly or through the vendor HAL; Build graph connects rules, registers and code. How it gets the manual. When you import a TI or ST project with the Import Project wizard, Noyce IDE identifies the part, downloads its reference manual and indexes it. You can also index a manual you already have with Choose PDF…, and rebuild the index with Re-index. How to use it Type a register or field name in the search box, for example GPIOAFSEL. Select the register to see what the manual says about it, its offset and reset value, the page it is documented on, every base address it appears at, and its bit fields. Switch to Rules to see the documented constraints for that register, such as unlock sequences and commit-control requirements. Link code finds where your firmware writes each register, directly or through the vendor HAL, and Build graph connects registers, rules and code. The manual and the index are stored in .noyce/manuals/ and .noyce/knowledge/.

Flash and RAM use by module, symbol and section, worst-case stack depth, and what changed since the last build. Open it with Noyce Hardware: Open Firmware Memory & Stack. Firmware Memory on the Canister copy after a Debug build with TI armcl: FLASH 42.5 KB of 1 MB and SRAM 101.8 KB of 256 KB, with the per-module breakdown. TI does not record stack usage, so worst-case depth reads not established. What it needs: a GNU linker map (-Wl,-Map=<name>.map) or TI Arm linker map from a build of the project. GNU builds need -fstack-usage .su files for worst-case stack depth. 01FROM THE BUILD02FROM THE SOURCE03ANALYSIS04WHAT YOU SEELinker mapGNU ld -Map · TI armcl --map_file.su filesGCC -fstack-usage frame per functionTI writes noneCall graphparsed from your C sourcesMemory budgetregions · sections · modules · symbolsStack depthdeepest path from each root:main · interrupt handlers · tasksvs the linker reservationBudget per regionwithin / over budgetStack checksworst case · margins · pathcannot be boundedRecursion · indirect calls · missing frames · allocanamed as such — never guessedBaselineSet as baseline · .noyce/firmware-memory/compared withSince last buildsymbols added, grown, shrunkWithout .su files (any TI build) the stack section shows the configured stack size and says the worst case is not established. The linker map gives the memory budget per region, section, module and symbol. GCC stack-usage records and a call graph parsed from your sources give the deepest stack path from main, each interrupt handler and each task, checked against the linker reservation. What cannot be bounded is named, not guessed. A baseline gives the change since the last build. Tabs show Modules, Symbols, Sections, Stack roots and Since last build, with a budget card for each memory region. The first build becomes the baseline that later builds are compared against. NoteFirmware Memory reads TI Arm linker maps too: memory regions, sections, per-function sizes and per-object totals. Build the project in CCS or in Build Pipeline so a .map exists. TI does not produce -fstack-usage records, so for a TI map the view shows the configured stack size and says the worst-case depth is not established.

The chip's package with every pin's function, taken from your project. Open it with Noyce Hardware: Open Pin Configurator, or open an STM32 .ioc file. Pin Configurator for the TM4C1294NCPDT (TQFP128, 128 pins), with the pin assignments reconstructed from the Canister firmware's TivaWare C source. STM32: the configuration is read from the .ioc, and edits are written back to it. TI Tiva: there is no .ioc, so Noyce IDE reconstructs the pin map from the TivaWare calls in your C source (GPIOPinConfigure, GPIOPinType…, SysCtlPeripheralEnable). The pin configuration is detected when the project opens; Detect Pin Config from Loaded Project re-scans on demand. Generate init code writes initialisation code for the current configuration.

The peripherals and pins your project uses, grouped by peripheral, with each pin's signal and the net label from your code. Open it with Noyce Hardware: Open Peripheral Registers. Peripherals & Pin Map on the Canister copy: 17 assigned GPIO pins, each with its signal and the label from the firmware, such as PL6 → AUTO24V_3V3_EN2. This view is derived from the pin configuration. It does not read registers from the target; for live values, use the Debug Probe and Memory View.

A CMSIS-SVD browser and decoder: look up any register's fields, or paste a value and see each field decoded. Open it with Noyce Hardware: Open Register Inspector. Register Inspector before an SVD is loaded: it shows a small built-in sample device until you load your part's SVD. Where the SVD comes from. When the project contains an SVD file, the view opens on it and says "Loaded from the workspace." It uses the file named in the noyce.agents.svd.path setting (absolute, or relative to the project folder), or else the first *.svd in the project outside node_modules, .git, out, dist and build. Files over 30 MB are not loaded. To use another file for this session, select Load .svd… and pick it (.svd or .xml). Then search for a peripheral or register, and paste a value into Decode Register Value to see every field. NoteWith no SVD in the project, the view opens on a small built-in sample device and says so, naming your part when it has detected it. Load your own SVD before trusting the field layout. The same SVD also powers register hovers and completions in the editor; see AI & agents.

Search a schematic PDF, extract a bill of materials from it, and see an inferred component graph. Open it from the Schematic + BoM tile. Schematic Viewer lists the PDFs it finds in the project; choose one or select Open PDF…. How to use it Pick a PDF from PDFs found in this project, or Open PDF…. The pages render; nothing is analysed yet. Select Analyze (or Find, which analyses first). Noyce IDE extracts every piece of text with its position: through LiteParse, with PaddleOCR on pages that have almost no text, when the desktop host provides them; otherwise with pdf.js and tesseract.js OCR in the window. The header then reads how many text items and parts it found. BoM opens the bill of materials built from the reference designators it found: quantity, class, value and designators. Select a designator to jump to it on the page. Graph opens the inferred component graph. Find (⌘F) searches every extracted word, net labels included. Open in BoM Studio hands the BoM over for distributor lookups and Excel export. The Canister controller schematic after Analyze: 1,674 text items and 222 parts, extracted with pdf.js. The Bill of Materials groups them by class with every designator; the title block is blurred here. The inferred component graph for the same sheet. Edges come from shared net labels and from parts placed close together. ImportantThe component graph is inferred from the layout, not parsed from a netlist: a NET edge joins parts near the same net label, and a dashed PROXIMITY edge joins parts placed close together. Treat it as a guide when reading the schematic, not as connectivity evidence.

Load a bill of materials from Excel or CSV, or take the one extracted from a schematic, and enrich each part with distributor data. Open it with Noyce Hardware: Open BoM Studio. BoM Studio: load an Excel or CSV BoM, or use the one from the Schematic Viewer. Distributor enrichment uses Mouser and DigiKey. Enter their credentials with these commands from the Command Palette. Each opens a password prompt, and what you type is stored in the system keychain (VS Code SecretStorage), not in your settings: Command What it asks for Noyce Parts: Set Mouser API Key… Your Mouser Search API key Noyce Parts: Set DigiKey Credentials… Your DigiKey API application's OAuth client ID, then its client secret. Both are kept in the keychain. Noyce Parts: Clear Distributor Credentials Nothing: it removes the Mouser and DigiKey credentials from the keychain after you confirm When no distributor is configured and a BoM is loaded, BoM Studio also shows Set Mouser API key… and Set DigiKey credentials… buttons that open the same prompts. The setting noyce.parts.preferredDistributor is mouser (default) or digikey: which one is asked first. The other is asked when the first has no answer. If only one is configured, it is used whatever this says. Each enriched row shows which distributor answered. The credentials never leave the extension host: they are not logged and are never passed to the BoM Studio page itself. NoteEarlier versions kept these credentials in the plain settings noyce.parts.mouser.apiKey, noyce.parts.digikey.clientId and noyce.parts.digikey.clientSecret. On the first start after updating, Noyce IDE moves any of them it finds (in User, Workspace or folder settings) into the keychain, removes them from every settings file they were in, and tells you once. A credential already in the keychain is kept. A value committed to a repository's .vscode/settings.json before the move is still in that repository's history, so rotate it. Export .xlsx and Export .csv write bom.xlsx or bom.csv to .noyce/bom/ in the project.

Decode an ARM Cortex-M HardFault from its fault registers. Open it from the HardFault Analyzer tile. Fault Analyzer on its built-in example dump, marked as an example: a precise BusFault, with the stacked exception frame, the fault status bits and recommendations. Paste the register dump from your debugger: CFSR, HFSR, BFAR, MMFAR and the stacked R0–PC and xPSR. Optionally load the build's .map so addresses resolve to function names. Select Decode Fault. The analyzer names the fault, explains each status bit, shows the exception frame, and recommends where to look. It decodes what you paste; it does not read faults from a running target.

A UART or USB serial console with real port access. Open it with ⌘⌥N then R. Serial Monitor: choose the port and baud rate (115200 by default), then Connect. Send text or hex. Debug with AI saves the session to .noyce/serial/latest.log and hands it to an agent with the question you ask.

Attach a debug probe through probe-rs, which is built into Noyce IDE. Open them with Noyce Hardware: Open Debug Probe and Open Memory View. Debug Probe with no probe on the USB bus. Connect an ST-Link, J-Link or CMSIS-DAP probe and it is listed here. Debug Probe lists connected probes, finds your chip in the probe-rs registry, attaches, and gives you halt, run, step, reset and reset-and-halt. It can also flash an image and verify it. Memory View reads live target memory once a probe is attached.

The STM32 Debug State view in the Noyce IDE sidebar shows, for the attached target: Probe Status: each probe on the USB bus, and whether a target is attached. When none is, select Attach Debug Probe. Core Registers: the core registers, with values that changed since the last read marked. Memory Watches: addresses you want to keep an eye on. Select + (Add Memory Watch), then enter either a hex address such as 0x20000000 or a symbol name such as adc_samples, then a label and a size in bytes. A symbol name is looked up in the project's GNU ld .map file, the newest one in the workspace, so build the project first. The size defaults to the symbol's size when the map gives it, and to 4 bytes when it does not; change it if the variable is larger. If the name is not in the map, the view says so and asks again. Each watch shows the bytes at that address in hex, with the symbol name in its label. Bytes that changed since the last read are marked. Watches are kept with the workspace; remove one with its × button. The view reads through probe-rs. While it is visible and a target is attached, it re-reads the core registers and memory watches every second. Set noyce.stm32.debug.refreshIntervalMs to change the interval (250 ms minimum), or to 0 to turn auto-refresh off. It also updates when you select Refresh, add or remove a watch, or attach or detach. A symbol is resolved to its address when you add the watch: after a rebuild that moves it, add the watch again. Watches read memory, not expressions.

A Modbus master over a serial port: choose the port, baud rate and slave ID, and read holding registers. Open it with Noyce Hardware: Open Modbus Monitor. NoteThe register table starts as an example register map and is labelled so. Replace the addresses and names with your device's register map. The serial connection is real.

Signal Viewer, Live Data Dashboard, HIL Test Runner, Energy Profiler and Data Recorder show generated data for demonstration, and each says so with a banner. Do not use their numbers as measurements. Data Recorder's export writes the generated samples to .noyce/recordings/. See Known limitations.

FPGA Workspace (⌘⌥N then F) and Synthesis Dashboard lay out what an FPGA flow will show: HDL sources, constraints, and a synthesis report with utilization, timing and power. WarningFPGA synthesis is not connected in this release. Run synthesis says that Vivado was not run, and the figures in both views are an example, marked as one, not results for your project.

Every function, file and macro in the project and how they connect, on one canvas. Open it from the Project Graph activity bar icon, its tile, or Noyce Project Graph: Open Project Graph. Project Graph on the Canister copy: 92 functions, 23 files and 59 macros. The entry flow from main is highlighted; the side panels show code ownership, libraries and the selected node's neighbourhood. Read it like this Entry flow starts at main and follows the call edges, so you see how the firmware boots and what its loop calls. Code ownership separates your project code from vendor code (TivaWare or STM32 HAL) and generated or boot code. Select a node to see its callers, callees and the macros it uses. Focus Entry recentres on the entry flow; Reset View fits everything. Cluster by groups the graph to answer different questions: Cluster by Answers Directory How is the code laid out on disk? Layer What is application, middleware, vendor SDK? Language Where are the C, assembly and headers? Ownership, Library What is ours and what is the vendor's? Community Which functions form tightly connected groups (Louvain)? Blast radius What is affected if the selected function changes?

A C4 architecture model built from the code. Open it from the Architecture activity bar icon, its tile, or ⌘⌥N then Y. System Architecture on the Canister copy: 23 files and 92 functions grouped into 3 subsystems with 111 relationships, shown at the Containers level. Choose the analysis mode. Static builds the model from the code graph alone, with no model. AI and Hybrid also ask your model to name and group the subsystems; if the model is unavailable, the static result is shown and labelled as such. Select Analyze. Move between levels with the tabs: Context, Containers, Components, Code, Dependencies, Data Flow and Embedded. Select a node for its details. Export the model as Structurizr DSL, Mermaid, Markdown, Draw.io, JSON, SVG, PNG or PDF, or Save to .noyce to keep it with the project for the SDD.

High-Level Design draws a Mermaid architecture diagram of the project with a local model. It sends up to 60 source files in one request of about 14,000 characters, shared between them: small files go in whole and larger ones contribute their opening lines (includes, types and declarations), so one large file cannot crowd out the rest. It draws the diagram, and saves it to .noyce/diagrams/hld.json; the next time you open it with unchanged source, the saved diagram is shown without asking the model again. Scroll to zoom and drag to pan. Regenerate draws it again, Export .md saves it as a Markdown file with the Mermaid block, and Open in Architecture Analyzer returns to the C4 model. High-Level Design on the Canister copy, drawn by Ornith from 23 source files: boot and initialisation, NVM and IP restore, the UDP and RS485 mailboxes, the H-Bridge controller, discrete I/O, the auto-sequence state machine and the safe state on loss of communication. One line the model wrote was not valid Mermaid; the notice above the diagram shows it. If a line the model wrote is not valid Mermaid, that line is left out, the rest of the diagram is drawn, and a notice above it shows the line. Regenerate asks the model again. NoteHigh-Level Design works with any local model (LM Studio, vLLM through the LM Studio provider, Ollama or Open WebUI), and its badge names the model used. The C4 model and Archify work with any model.

An architecture diagram of the open project, drawn by your model and checked before it is shown. Open it with Noyce: Archify Diagrams or the Archify button in System Architecture. Archify on the Canister copy: the controller's subsystems (UDP and RS485 intercom, system time, auto sequence, DI/DO card control, flash) and the paths between them, generated by the local model. The model writes the diagram in Archify's structured format, Noyce IDE validates it, and only a valid diagram is rendered. Pick the diagram type and select Regenerate to draw it again. Diagrams are saved to .noyce/diagrams/ and can be placed in DO-178C documents and their Word exports.

Ask a question in plain language and get the most relevant code and documentation. Open it from the tile or Noyce: Semantic Search. Semantic Search with the Canister index built: 300 chunks of code and documentation, ready to query. Set an embedding server in AI Models → Embeddings and select Save & test. See Connect a model. Select Build / Rebuild index. The index is stored in .noyce/rag/index.json. Type a question, for example "where is the RS485 packet checksum verified", and press Enter. The same index grounds the agents: relevant code is added to their prompts, so their answers cite your project. What a missing embedding model looks like: the server answered 404 because it does not serve text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5. The index is fine; the query cannot be embedded. ImportantBoth building the index and every query need the embedding model. If your model server only serves a chat model, queries fail as shown above. Point Embeddings at a server that serves an embedding model, and rebuild the index if you change models.
Every AI feature runs on the model you choose in AI Models. For the screenshots on this page that was Ornith (ornith-1.5-35b-a3b), served by vLLM on a machine on the local network.

A kanban board where agents work through tasks for this project. Open it with ⌘⌥N then O or Noyce AI: Open AI Orchestrator. The Orchestrator on the Canister copy: Ornith with a 262K context, up to 3 concurrent calls, and 88 cards in the sprint: 71 Annex A objectives to do and 17 documents waiting in Handover for review. 01THE BOARD.noyce/orchestrator-tasks.json, per projectBacklogone task per lineTo Doready for an agentIn Progressowned by an agentHandoverneeds operator reviewDoneyou review hereAgent + modelrole model or globalrunscodeChange setapprove to applydocs, evidence.noyce/ artifactsdrafts, never finalCards come from the backlog box, Generate via Orchestrator on the Compliance Dashboard, and DO-178C document authoring. A card moves from Backlog to To Do, In Progress, Handover and Done. While it is in progress an agent works it on its model, writing documents and evidence into .noyce as drafts and code as a change set. Handover is where you review the result. Reading the board The header shows the model in use, its context size, live token rate, and how many calls are running. It is a readout; choose models in Models. The strip shows concurrency, sprint progress, how many cards wait for your review, and the handoff chain of the 15 agents. The columns: To Do (ready for an agent), In Progress (an agent owns it), Handover (the agent is done and you need to review it), Done. Status / By agent switches the grouping. Adding work Type tasks in Backlog, one per line. Prefix a line with an agent to route it (coder: implement voltage clamp) and add [high] for priority. Then Add to sprint or Add to backlog. Generate via Orchestrator on the Compliance Dashboard adds one card per open objective. Authoring a DO-178C document adds a card for that document. Running it Run next runs the next card. Run sprint works through the sprint. Run full pipeline runs the multi-agent pipeline on an objective you type in the box next to it. Auto-run keeps the sprint moving as cards finish. Agent output opens one tab per agent with its streamed output, its reasoning, and the actions it took. See Agent Output. What agents produce. Documents and evidence are written into .noyce/ as drafts for you to review. Code is never written to your files directly: with Auto-apply agent code off you choose Stage all as change set in the agent's output; with it on, the change set is staged for you. Either way it waits in Evidence Records → Change sets for a person to approve. The board is saved per project in .noyce/orchestrator-tasks.json, so cards from one project never appear in another.

Agent Typical work System Designer Breaks a goal into tasks and design. Software Engineer Writes code (route with coder:). Test Engineer Writes tests. Code Reviewer Reviews changes. Doc Generator Drafts documents and objective evidence. Traceability Monitor Checks trace links. MISRA Code Fixer, CBMC Fixer, CodeQL Fixer Propose fixes for findings, as change sets. Compliance Author Writes compliance evidence. Doc Author, Doc Reviewer Author and review DO-178C document sections. UI/UX Designer, Frontend Developer, API Integrator General roles, not firmware-specific. Give any agent its own model in AI Models → Agent Role Assignment.

A chat panel in the secondary sidebar, with a choice of agent persona. Open it with ⌘⇧A or Noyce AI: Open Agents Chat (⌘⌃I). Switch agent with ⌘K ⌘A, attach a file with ⌘⇧O, search the thread with ⌘F, and stop a reply with ⌘.. Agent History keeps every thread, with export, delete and re-run. Edits an agent makes from the chat can be undone with Revert Last Agent Edit or Revert All Agent Edits. In the Code-OSS Chat view, the @noyce participant answers in agent, ask or edit mode and has /fix, /test, /explain and /trace.
These features use the Coder agent and the model assigned to it.

Select the code to change, or leave the cursor on a line to change only that line. Press ⌘K ⌘I (Edit Inline…) and describe the change. The proposal appears in the file: the old lines in red, the new lines in green below them. Enter accepts it, Esc rejects it. Accepting saves the file, records the edit in the audit trail, and adds a checkpoint, so Revert Last Agent Edit can undo it. Your project rules that match the file are sent with the request. Only one inline edit can be open at a time. Note⌘K ⌘I replaces the Code-OSS Show Hover shortcut. Rebind either in Keyboard Shortcuts if you need both.

Both are off by default. Inline completions (noyce.agents.inline.enabled) show ghost text as you type. Tab accepts. Next edit (noyce.agents.inline.nextEdit.enabled, which also needs completions on) predicts the next change you are likely to make elsewhere in the file, after you accept a completion or when you run Predict Next Edit. When a prediction is ready, ⌘⌥] (Jump to Next Edit) moves the cursor there and shows it as ghost text; Tab accepts it and Esc dismisses it. Typing in the file discards the prediction. noyce.agents.inline.maxLines (12) caps how long a suggestion can be.

Composer (⌘⌥K) reviews an agent's changes across several files, hunk by hunk. Accepted hunks are staged as a change set. CodeLens actions above functions: Refactor with Coder, Audit MISRA with Reviewer, Generate Tests with Tester. Generate Driver from Datasheet (⌘⌥D) drafts a driver from a datasheet you attach. Fix with Noyce appears as a quick fix on MISRA diagnostics. See Review AI changes. Register hovers: when the workspace has a CMSIS-SVD file, hovering a peripheral register in C or C++ shows its description and fields, and completions are grounded in it. Noyce IDE uses noyce.agents.svd.path or else the first *.svd in the workspace; run Reload SVD File after replacing it.

Kind Command Stored in Project rules: standing instructions, such as your coding standard Create Project Rule, Show Project Rules NOYCE.md and .noyce/rules/*.md Notepads: reusable notes you can attach Create Notepad…, Show Notepads… .noyce/notepads/*.md Memories: facts the agents keep about the project Remember This…, Show Project Memories, Clear Project Memories .noyce/memories.md Rules and memories are added to every request, up to noyce.agents.rules.maxChars (6,000) and noyce.agents.memories.maxChars (4,000) characters. In the agents chat, type @ to attach context to one message: Mention Attaches @file, @folder A file (up to noyce.agents.context.maxFileBytes, 32 KB) or a folder listing @symbol A function or type and its neighbours from the code graph @codebase The most relevant code from the Semantic Search index @git Your staged changes and the last commit @requirement A requirement's shall statement, from your requirement documents @docs Matching passages from the project's docs/ folder @notepad One of your notepads @serial The end of the latest Serial Monitor capture @web An online search. Off by default; turn on noyce.agents.context.web.enabled When the Semantic Search index is built, relevant code from it is added to agent prompts as well.

Edit Agent System Prompt… lists the agents and shows which ones have a custom prompt. Pick one to copy its built-in prompt into .noyce/agents/prompts/<agent>.md and open it; your edited copy is used from then on. Delete the file to go back to the built-in prompt. Prompts saved by earlier versions in .noyce-agents/prompts/<agent>.md are still used when there is no copy under .noyce/. When you pick one of those agents, you are asked whether to move its file to the new location; nothing is deleted unless you choose Move.

Build, flash, watch the output, propose a repair, and build again, until the output matches what you expect or the attempts run out. Open it with ⌘⌥N then V. Each proposed repair is staged as a change set; it is never written straight to your files. The loop needs noyce.agents.enableShell, and offers to turn it on for the workspace.

Fix Build Errors with AI sends the errors in the Problems list, with a few lines of source around each, to the Coder agent and asks for a patch. A diff opens for each file, then you choose Stage all fixes, Stage per file… or Discard. Nothing is written to your source: staged fixes wait as a change set in Evidence Records for you to approve. Warnings are included only if noyce.agents.buildfix.includeWarnings is on.

Generate Commit Message in the Source Control title bar writes a message for your staged changes (or all changes when nothing is staged) into the commit message box, following Conventional Commits unless you turn off noyce.agents.scm.conventionalCommits. Nothing is committed for you. Explain My Changes, next to it, opens a plain-language summary of the same diff. In the terminal, ⌘K opens Generate Terminal Command (replacing the Code-OSS Clear shortcut there). Describe what you want; the command comes back with Insert into terminal, Insert and run and Copy. Commands that look dangerous never offer Insert and run. Explain Terminal Failure explains the output you have selected in the terminal, or output you paste.

Find these in Settings under Noyce Agents. Every feature setting ending in .enabled turns its feature off when cleared. Setting Default What it does noyce.agents.enableShell off Lets agents run shell commands in the workspace (120-second limit). Needed for verifyCommand and the Firmware Validation Loop. noyce.agents.verifyCommand empty The command an agent runs when it checks its own work, such as your build or test command. Without it, or with the shell off, the check uses the editor's diagnostics only. noyce.agents.auditCapture on Records agent file edits and checks in the audit trail, .noyce/audit-ledger.json. noyce.agents.gemini.fallbackChain Gemini 3.1 Pro … 2.5 Flash-Lite When a Gemini model reports a quota or rate limit, it rests for the time Gemini asks (or 60 seconds) and the next model in the list is used. noyce.agents.scm.maxDiffChars 24,000 How much of a diff is sent for commit messages and summaries. noyce.agents.buildfix.contextLines, maxFiles 6, 8 Source lines around each error, and how many files (those with the most errors) are sent. noyce.agents.firmwareLoop.* The loop's build, flash and observe commands, success pattern, attempts (3), time limit (120 s) and auto-apply (off). noyce.chat.enableShell off Lets the @noyce participant in the Chat view run shell commands. Separate from noyce.agents.enableShell.

Noyce IDE never writes generated files into your source tree. Everything it produces for a project (analysis results, documents, evidence, the audit trail, agent state) goes into a .noyce/ folder at the project root.

Commit the life-cycle data in .noyce/ with the project: documents, requirements, review and verification records, compliance runs, change sets, configuration, and the audit ledger. The IDE does not commit these files for you. The IDE writes .noyce/.gitignore when .noyce/ is first created and checks for it when a workspace folder opens. It ignores only these regenerable caches and scratch files: gitignoreCopy/build/ /codeql/db-* /codeql/result-* /codeql/mirror-* /rag/ /manuals/ /knowledge/ /serial/ /architecture/model-cache.json /audit-ledger.json.tmp.* Downloaded vendor manuals can be downloaded again. The knowledge index, register code links, and graph are regenerated from the manual and project sources. Kept CodeQL evidence (codeql/last-scan-*.sarif) remains committable. The IDE replaces its legacy .gitignore header followed by a single *, but preserves user-edited ignore files. It also removes the legacy .noyce/ entry it wrote to .git/info/exclude; only .codegraph/ is excluded there. Other project or global ignore rules may still prevent files from appearing in Source Control.

This is the folder from the Canister Main Controller copy used for these docs, plus the locations each surface writes to once it has been used. Folders appear only when the feature that owns them has run. textCopy.noyce/ ├── .gitignore ignores only regenerable caches and scratch ├── audit-ledger.json hash-chained audit trail ├── orchestrator-tasks.json the Orchestrator board for this project ├── architecture/ System Architecture model cache and exports ├── diagrams/ Archify diagrams, High-Level Design ├── compliance/ │ ├── article-do-178c.json framework, assurance level and objective article │ ├── evidence-snapshot.json the latest dashboard scan │ ├── static-analysis.json stored analysis findings │ ├── annex-a-licensed.json your licensed Annex A table, once imported │ └── evidence/ generated evidence write-ups ├── annex-a/ objective map and objective text ├── compliance-runs/ one folder per compliance run, plus index.json ├── certification/ certification packages (.md, .html, .json) ├── documents/ │ ├── index.json the document register │ ├── PSAC-001.sdoc … each life-cycle document, and its .docx export │ ├── proposals/ agent-drafted decisions awaiting review │ ├── history/ frozen revisions with their content hash │ └── set-baseline.json the declared document-set baseline ├── templates/ your corporate .docx template settings ├── requirements/ imported system requirements, low-level requirements ├── process/ roster, reviews, problem reports, CCB, MISRA deviations ├── change-sets/ staged code changes awaiting approval ├── verification/ test cases, results, CBMC runs, target test runs ├── coverage/ measured MC/DC per driver ├── manuals/ the downloaded reference manual (PDF) ├── knowledge/ the indexed register knowledge base ├── rag/ the Semantic Search index └── rules/ notepads/ memories.md context you give the agents

Delete What happens rag/, architecture/model-cache.json, knowledge/ Rebuilt the next time you use the view. Re-indexing a manual or the workspace takes a few minutes. compliance/evidence-snapshot.json Rebuilt by the next dashboard scan. documents/, process/, audit-ledger.json, compliance-runs/ Lost for good. These are your records: issued documents, human reviews and the audit trail. Deleting the whole folder returns the project to a fresh state. Your source files are unaffected.

Noyce IDE is built on one rule: a surface either shows what it measured on your project, or it says it has nothing. This page lists every place where that rule has a caveat, so you are never surprised by it.

The certification package is sealed, not signed. Sections are SHA-256 hashed and the digest is anchored to the audit trail; there is no private-key signature. Annex A objective text is not included. It is licensed by RTCA. Import your own copy; until then plans and summaries stay marked DRAFT. Object Code Traceability needs an analysis produced outside the app. The view suggests npm run socta, a script in the Noyce IDE source repository that the installed app does not include. External requirement tools are not connected. Jama Connect and IBM DOORS Next do not sync. Export ReqIF or CSV from them and import the file in Requirements Authoring.

CodeQL scans of TI projects are buildless. CodeQL cannot trace the TI armcl compiler, so the scan reads the sources with guessed include paths and defines. The dashboard says so, and a count of 0 from such a scan is not conclusive. See Code Scanning. Semantic Search needs a server that serves embeddings. A chat-only server, such as a vLLM instance serving one generative model, answers /v1/embeddings with 404.

Builds cover TI Code Composer Studio and STM32CubeIDE projects. ⇧⌘B, the status bar items and the Noyce build tasks appear only when the folder has a CCS .cproject. A TI build links only with armcl and a linker command file whose libraries all resolve; otherwise it compiles only, and there is no .map for Firmware Memory. Team Activity is always empty and Review Workflow cannot sync: no collaboration backend is connected. Build Status and the Build view's History tab differ. Build Status lists your last 10 builds, TI CCS and STM32. The Build view's History tab still shows only the latest CCS build of each configuration. No CI system is connected.

Simulated data. Signal Viewer, Live Data Dashboard, HIL Test Runner, Energy Profiler and Data Recorder show generated data under a "simulated" banner. Do not use their numbers as measurements. Fault Analyzer opens on a built-in example dump, marked as an example, until you paste your own. It does not read faults from a live target. Register Inspector opens on a sample device when the project has no .svd file and you have not loaded one. When it has detected your part it says the sample is not that part. Modbus Monitor starts with an example register map, labelled as one. The serial connection is real. Firmware Memory cannot establish worst-case stack depth for TI builds. TI's compiler does not write -fstack-usage records, so the view shows the configured stack size instead. Peripheral Registers is derived from the pin configuration, not read from the target. FPGA synthesis is not connected. FPGA Workspace and Synthesis Dashboard show an example report, marked as one, and Run synthesis builds nothing.
Three Orchestrator agents are general web roles (UI/UX Designer, Frontend Developer, API Integrator) and are not specific to firmware. There is no in-app updater. See Update.

These docs describe the current release. If you are still on v2.0.7, these behave differently: Assurance level. The level in Settings → Compliance Standards is not saved, and Compliance Run, Certification Readiness, Data & Control Coupling, MC/DC Coverage and Evidence Records assess Level A whatever the project's level. Set the level in the Compliance Dashboard header. Annotation Navigator labels every @req tag Verified, whether or not a test exists. Read it as "tag found". Classified mode has no effect: no feature reads the toggle. Cloud API keys are kept in the IDE's local web storage, not the keychain. Build. There are no build tasks, status bar items or ⇧⌘B; build from the Build Pipeline view, which shows a stage list, a generated YAML tab and log lines instead of real artifacts. Firmware Memory reads GNU ld map files only, not TI armcl maps. CodeQL on a TI project extracts no files and reports 0 alerts. Test Explorer does not record Run All results; Analyze with AI Agent on a failed test does nothing. The Firmware Validation Loop stops after the first staged repair. STM32 memory reads, RTT and the Debug State view cannot attach a probe themselves; attach in the Debug Probe view. High-Level Design draws only with a Gemma model on LM Studio, draws its boxes without labels, packs source files in name order so the first large file can take the whole request, and shows nothing at all if one line of the model's diagram is invalid. Document Reader offers Edit on generated documents, and the edits are lost when the document is rebuilt from its source. Evidence Records judges verification-case independence by name, and Remove on the roster does not ask for confirmation. Noyce: Import Project in the Command Palette only picks a folder, Project Templates create an in-memory demo, and ⌘⌥N M and ⌘⌥N P each open two views. Data Recorder shows no "simulated" banner, and Modbus Monitor shows an example device's name ("Dynamo Modbus Explorer"). The Trace agent's output tab shows fixed coverage figures (100% traced, 96% covered) that are not measured. Fix with Noyce asks the model for the whole file, so a fix can rewrite code far from the finding, such as the file header; the dialog lists the entire file instead of the change. BoM Studio and Data Recorder exports do not download inside the IDE window. FPGA Workspace: Run synthesis reports "Synthesis complete" without running anything, over a fixed example report with no banner. Load demo project on the start tab opens an error. Register Inspector never opens the project's own SVD file; load it with Load .svd… every time. Pipeline Status in the sidebar is empty, or reads "Pipeline idle". It does not list your builds. The sidebar view listing serial ports is called Workspace Signals, and the status bar reads No Probe when there are no serial ports; it has nothing to do with debug probes. Some agent commands appear in the Command Palette as "Noyce Agents: Noyce: …". Mouser and DigiKey credentials are plain settings, not stored in the keychain. Custom agent prompts live in .noyce-agents/prompts/. The current release reads them from there too, and offers to move them to .noyce/agents/prompts/. STM32 Debug State memory watches update only when you select Refresh, and take hex addresses only.

sections.h: macOS says the app is damaged or from an unidentified developer
sections.t: The disk-image build is not notarized. Clear the quarantine flag, then open the app again: TerminalCopyxattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Noyce IDE.app" Homebrew and the one-line installer do this for you.
The beta installer is not code-signed yet. Select More info, then Run anyway.

sections.h: The window is blank or a view stops responding
sections.t: Run Developer: Reload Window from the Command Palette. Your open project and its .noyce/ data are kept.

sections.h: A panel says to configure a model first
sections.t: The DO-178C Documents panel and the agents need a model before they can draft anything. Open Noyce AI: Open AI Models, select a model and confirm its server URL. See Connect a model.

sections.h: Semantic Search says "Embedding request failed with status 404"
sections.t: The full message looks like this: textCopySearch failed Embedding request failed with status 404: model 'text-embedding-nomic-embed-text-v1.5' is not being served right now; available: ['ornith-1.5-35b-a3b'] The embedding server does not serve the embedding model, usually because it is the chat server and serves only a chat model. The available list shows what it does serve. In AI Models → Embeddings, point the embedding server at one that serves an embedding model, select Save & test (it reports the vector size it received), then Build / Rebuild index. A vLLM server started for one generative model has no embeddings endpoint at all.

sections.h: A local model returns empty or cut-off answers
sections.t: The server is probably running with a smaller context window than the model supports, or does not report it. Set Context window (tokens) for that model in AI Models to what the server actually runs. With LM Studio, also check the context length you loaded the model with.

sections.h: Cannot reach a vLLM server on another machine
sections.t: Use the LM Studio provider and enter the server's address, for example http://<host>:8000. If the server was started with --api-key, enter the key in API key (only if the server requires one).

sections.h: An STM32 build stops with "cannot read spec file 'nano.specs'"
sections.t: The arm-none-eabi-gcc being used has no C library. Homebrew's arm-none-eabi-gcc formula is like this. Install the Arm GNU Toolchain, or use STM32CubeIDE's, and set noyce.stm32.armToolchainPath to its bin folder. A compiler in that folder wins over the one on PATH. Noyce STM32: Validate Toolchain confirms which compiler is used. See Import and build.

sections.h: An STM32 build says "multiple target patterns" or "No rule to make target"
sections.t: The makefiles in Debug/ were generated by STM32CubeIDE on another computer and name its paths, often C:/…. Regenerate them in STM32CubeIDE on this computer, or use Build with a generated makefile in the Build view. See Import and build.

sections.h: Code that built in STM32CubeIDE fails with "incompatible pointer type"
sections.t: GCC 14 and later treat some former warnings as errors, among them incompatible pointer types. Build with the GCC version the project declares (STM32CubeIDE shows it under the project's MCU toolchain settings), and fix the warnings on purpose.
They come from the built-in heuristic scan, which runs when no analyzer is installed. Install cppcheck (brew install cppcheck on macOS) and select Scan again.

MC/DC needs LLVM/Clang 18 or newer (clang, llvm-profdata, llvm-cov). gcov cannot measure MC/DC. Install LLVM with brew install llvm on macOS or the LLVM installer on Windows, then run the measurement again.

sections.h: Formal Verification or Code Scanning says no run yet
sections.t: CBMC and CodeQL are not bundled. Select Install CBMC or Install CodeQL in the view, or install them yourself and make sure they are on your PATH. See Optional tools.

sections.h: Firmware Memory says there is no link map
sections.t: Firmware Memory reads GNU and TI Arm linker .map files from a build. For a GNU build, create a map file (-Wl,-Map=<name>.map) and add -fstack-usage for worst-case stack depth. For a TI Arm build, build the project in CCS or Build Pipeline so the .map exists.

The reference manual is downloaded when you import a project with the Import Project wizard, which needs a network connection. Import the project again with the wizard while online, or select Choose PDF… in Register Knowledge to index a manual you already have.

sections.h: Hardware views say the Noyce IDE service is not running
sections.t: Serial Monitor, the Serial Ports view, Debug Probe, Memory View and STM32 Debug State all talk to the Noyce IDE service (noyce-core) that ships inside the app. The status bar shows its state as Noyce: ok. If it is not running, use Developer: Reload Window. The STM32 commands and STM32 Debug State start their own copy of the service; to have them use a noyce-core you built yourself, set noyce.sidecar.command to its path and arguments, for example ["/path/to/noyce-core"]. Leave it empty to use the bundled one. The rest of the IDE always uses the bundled service.

sections.h: My reviews and documents are not in git
sections.t: Reviews, documents, requirements, verification records, compliance runs, configuration, change sets, and the audit ledger belong in version control. The IDE writes .noyce/.gitignore when the folder is first created; it ignores /build/, /codeql/db-*, /codeql/result-*, /codeql/mirror-*, /rag/, /manuals/, /knowledge/, /serial/, /architecture/model-cache.json, and /audit-ledger.json.tmp.* only. Reopen the project to replace an old IDE-generated ignore file containing only the IDE header and *. User-edited ignore files are preserved. If records are still missing from Source Control, run git check-ignore -v .noyce/documents/index.json (or the path of a missing record) to find the rule hiding them. Check project and global ignore rules as well as .git/info/exclude. Add and commit the records you need to retain. See The .noyce folder.

sections.h: A change set says it is stale
sections.t: A file it changes was edited after the change set was gated. Nothing was written. Propose the fix again on the current code. See Review AI changes.
Open an issue with your Noyce IDE version (Noyce: About Noyce IDE), your OS, and what you expected to happen.
